overall: Atlanta is running notably behind the seasonal heating curve as of 10 AM ET, with the temperature only at 78.8°F under a heavily overcast sky (BKN, 100% cloud fraction, ceiling just 274m). Despite a positive velocity of +1.6°F/hr, the thick low cloud deck is suppressing solar insolation and limiting the warming rate. Afternoon convective activity (40% PoP after 1 PM) adds further uncertainty about how much additional warming is achievable before storms potentially cap or erode the daily high.
forecast_obs_notes: Models show meaningful disagreement: ECMWF is the cool outlier at 83.8°F, the NBM blends to 86.6°F, and the HRRR is the aggressive warm outlier at 88.7°F. The NWS text forecast of 89°F aligns with the HRRR but requires substantial cloud clearing and uninterrupted heating through the early afternoon — a scenario the current overcast conditions make uncertain. The META model (most reliable) peaks its probability mass in the 88-89°F bucket (26.8%) followed by 90-91°F (23.6%), but these bullish outcomes depend heavily on timely cloud erosion.
max_temp_prediction: From 78.8°F at 10 AM ET with ~4.5 hours to the expected peak near 14:30 ET, sustained warming at the observed ~1.6-1.8°F/hr rate would yield roughly 86-87°F — consistent with the NBM and the intraday model's dual probability peaks at 86-87F and 88-89F. The HRRR/NWS scenario of 88-89°F requires a meaningful cloud break and acceleration in the warming rate that the current thick overcast and low ceiling make uncertain. Factoring in the thunderstorm risk as a capping/cooling mechanism and the current suppressed trajectory, confidence leans toward the 86-88°F zone with moderate uncertainty; 87-88°F is the most defensible central estimate.
